world.title: Indian man gets 19 years for plot to kill Sikh activist
world.summary: A U.S. federal judge sentenced Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 235 months in prison on Nov. 20 for his role in a murder-for-hire plot against Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, a U.S.-Canadian lawyer and Sikh separatist activist in New York. Prosecutors said Gupta worked with Indian government employee Vikash Yadav, who remains
world.content: A U.S. federal judge sentenced Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 235 months in prison on Nov. 20 for his role in a murder-for-hire plot against Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, a U.S.-Canadian lawyer and Sikh separatist activist in New York. Prosecutors said Gupta worked with Indian government employee Vikash Yadav, who remains outside U.S. custody, to arrange a $100,000 killing; a $15,000 advance went to an undercover Drug Enforcement Administration officer posing as a hitman. India denies government involvement. Prosecutors cited Gupta’s messages about Hardeep Singh Nijjar, a Sikh leader shot dead in British Columbia in June 2023; Canada has separately accused India of links to Nijjar’s killing, which India also denies. Gupta pleaded guilty in February 2026 to murder-for-hire, conspiracy and money-laundering charges. Pannun urged Canada to use evidence from the U.S. case in its Nijjar investigation, while the Royal Canadian Mounted Police said it could not discuss investigative steps or cooperation with international partners. Four Indian men charged in Nijjar’s killing are awaiting trial in British Columbia. The trial is not expected to begin until 2028.
world.image_alt: Indian man gets 19 years for plot to kill Sikh activist

world.title: Paris court sentences three officers for racist beating of music producer
world.summary: A Paris criminal court on Nov. 20 convicted three police officers of intentionally beating Black music producer Michel Zecler and found racism an aggravating factor in the 2020 assault. Each received a five-year sentence, with three to four years suspended. One officer will serve the remaining year under electronic mon
world.content: A Paris criminal court on Nov. 20 convicted three police officers of intentionally beating Black music producer Michel Zecler and found racism an aggravating factor in the 2020 assault. Each received a five-year sentence, with three to four years suspended. One officer will serve the remaining year under electronic monitoring; the other two are to enter prison. The court also found them guilty of falsifying a police report and barred all three from serving in the police again. The officers stopped Zecler outside his Paris studio on Nov. 21, 2020, saying he was not wearing a required mask. Security footage showed them beating him and contradicted their claim that he attacked them. The court found Zecler’s consistent account of hearing racial slurs credible. The officers admitted the beating and false report but denied racist intent. Zecler suffered head and facial injuries and a ruptured biceps tendon and could not work for 45 days. The verdict followed a two-week trial that began in early November. Prosecutors had sought prison terms of four to six years.
world.image_alt: Paris court sentences three officers for racist beating of music producer

world.title: Trump urges Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang despite board rejection
world.summary: President Donald Trump on Friday urged Nvidia to reinstate co-founder Jensen Huang, who resigned as chief executive on Nov. 12 after reports of extramarital relationships, including one with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud company Megaspeed suspected by U.S. officials of ties to Chinese intelli
world.content: President Donald Trump on Friday urged Nvidia to reinstate co-founder Jensen Huang, who resigned as chief executive on Nov. 12 after reports of extramarital relationships, including one with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud company Megaspeed suspected by U.S. officials of ties to Chinese intelligence. Trump called Huang a brilliant technology leader and said he should apologize before returning. Huang has said he would be willing to return. Allegations that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy remain disputed, and China has rejected them. Nvidia’s board has ruled out a return. Board Chair Harvey Jones said directors unanimously accepted Huang’s resignation and do not intend to reinstate him. Trump also said he discussed Huang with Chinese President Xi Jinping during their meeting in Shenzhen this week, contradicting Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who said the issue did not come up. A Commerce Department rule issued this week seeks to stop Chinese companies from renting access to advanced U.S. chips and servers through data centers in other countries. Huang has agreed to testify at a public Senate hearing, according to an aide to Republican Sen. Tim Scott.
world.image_alt: Trump urges Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang despite board rejection

world.title: Denmark expels Russian defence attaché after alleged plot against rapper
world.summary: Denmark on Nov. 20 ordered Russia’s defence attaché to leave within seven days after its Security and Intelligence Service (PET) accused Russian intelligence of planning to kill Ukrainian-American rapper Kyivstoner, whose real name is Albert Vasiliev, at a concert near Copenhagen. Danish authorities say police stopped
world.content: Denmark on Nov. 20 ordered Russia’s defence attaché to leave within seven days after its Security and Intelligence Service (PET) accused Russian intelligence of planning to kill Ukrainian-American rapper Kyivstoner, whose real name is Albert Vasiliev, at a concert near Copenhagen. Danish authorities say police stopped a car near the venue on Sept. 25 and found firearms and knives. Two Danish men face attempted-murder and foreign-intelligence charges and deny wrongdoing. The concert was cancelled. PET says the suspects had links to the outlawed Danish gang Loyal to Familia and that Russian intelligence planned the operation. Denmark summoned Russia’s ambassador and is pressing for European restrictions on non-essential visas for Russian citizens. Officials say existing Schengen visas issued by other countries can still allow travel to Denmark. Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen said Copenhagen would not sever diplomatic ties, while Russian officials rejected the accusation and promised a response.
world.image_alt: Denmark expels Russian defence attaché after alleged plot against rapper

world.title: COP31 talks extend into weekend as nations clash over fossil fuels
world.summary: The COP31 United Nations climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, ran past their scheduled Friday close, with nearly 200 countries still divided over a draft agreement and negotiations continuing into Saturday. A revised draft removed any mention of fossil fuels and dropped a proposed $120 billion annual adaptation-finance ta
world.content: The COP31 United Nations climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, ran past their scheduled Friday close, with nearly 200 countries still divided over a draft agreement and negotiations continuing into Saturday. A revised draft removed any mention of fossil fuels and dropped a proposed $120 billion annual adaptation-finance target for developing countries. The draft instead backs a voluntary goal of raising electricity’s share of global final energy use to 35% by 2035, but does not require that electricity to come from renewable sources. France, Panama and other countries are pressing to restore a clear commitment to move away from fossil fuels; oil and gas producers have opposed that language. Delegates approved technical decisions at a late Friday plenary but left the main political agreement unresolved. COP31 President Murat Kurum, Turkey’s environment minister, said a new draft was expected Saturday as negotiators continued discussions on fossil fuels, climate finance and carbon-capture proposals.
world.image_alt: COP31 talks extend into weekend as nations clash over fossil fuels

world.title: AI sell-off erases Nasdaq gains after Anthropic’s record IPO
world.summary: A global technology-stock sell-off deepened on Friday, Nov. 20, as shares in artificial-intelligence company Anthropic fell 8.5% in their first full day of trading, closing at $88.91 after briefly reaching $115.10 on debut. The retreat followed the company’s record public offering. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.3%, erasi
world.content: A global technology-stock sell-off deepened on Friday, Nov. 20, as shares in artificial-intelligence company Anthropic fell 8.5% in their first full day of trading, closing at $88.91 after briefly reaching $115.10 on debut. The retreat followed the company’s record public offering. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.3%, erasing its 2026 gains, while the S&P 500 fell 3.7% and entered correction territory, more than 10% below its October peak. Investors are questioning whether AI companies can earn enough to justify their enormous spending on chips and data centres. The sell-off also reflected concerns about possible US restrictions on the industry after Democrats’ midterm gains, tighter controls on Chinese firms’ remote access to Nvidia chips, and uncertainty at Nvidia after the reported departure of chief executive Jensen Huang and reports of a US accounting investigation. Losses spread to Asian and European markets, with chipmakers among the hardest hit. Market analysts said Anthropic’s share performance over the coming days and weeks would help gauge investor confidence in returns on AI spending.
world.image_alt: AI sell-off erases Nasdaq gains after Anthropic’s record IPO

world.title: Trump threatens tax on U.S. tech firms building AI data centres abroad
world.summary: President Donald Trump threatened a “tremendous tax” on U.S. technology companies that build artificial-intelligence data centres overseas, saying the facilities should remain in the United States to prevent China from gaining access to computing capacity. He gave no details on the proposed penalty and said he had not
world.content: President Donald Trump threatened a “tremendous tax” on U.S. technology companies that build artificial-intelligence data centres overseas, saying the facilities should remain in the United States to prevent China from gaining access to computing capacity. He gave no details on the proposed penalty and said he had not discussed it with his administration, leaving unclear how it could be imposed. Trump urged communities to accept domestic projects and negotiate payments or other benefits from developers. About three-quarters of U.S. voters opposed building a data centre in their community, with residents citing electricity prices and water use as concerns. The administration is tightening restrictions on remote access to advanced U.S. chips and servers to prevent Chinese firms from using computing capacity hosted in third countries. Technology companies are offering communities more transparency, environmental commitments and financial contributions to secure approval for projects.
world.image_alt: Trump threatens tax on U.S. tech firms building AI data centres abroad

world.title: European youth protests demand social spending as Italian strike disrupts services
world.summary: Students and workers demonstrated across more than 25 European countries on Friday, Nov. 20, over living costs, education, housing and military spending, while Italy’s largest trade union, the Italian General Confederation of Labour (CGIL), staged a 24-hour nationwide strike. Organizers said coordinated youth protests
world.content: Students and workers demonstrated across more than 25 European countries on Friday, Nov. 20, over living costs, education, housing and military spending, while Italy’s largest trade union, the Italian General Confederation of Labour (CGIL), staged a 24-hour nationwide strike. Organizers said coordinated youth protests were planned in about 400 cities; in Italy, demonstrations took place in more than 100 cities. Workers sought higher wages and stronger public services, while students in Germany and elsewhere opposed rearmament and a possible return to compulsory military service. Protesters also raised concerns about education funding, climate justice, housing costs and the war in Gaza. In Italy, the strike disrupted local transport, schools and some health services. The CGIL strike excluded rail and air travel, though a separate rail stoppage was scheduled to run until Saturday evening. CGIL leader Maurizio Landini said more than 1 million people joined demonstrations in Italy, while the Interior Ministry said it was too early to provide its own estimate. Police used pepper spray and made arrests at a youth protest in Vienna, and Leipzig police used water cannons after a demonstration there. Further airport-worker walkouts are scheduled for Sunday at Milan and Venice airports.
world.image_alt: European youth protests demand social spending as Italian strike disrupts services

business.title: Oil prices post third weekly loss as Gulf exports recover
business.summary: Oil prices fell for a third consecutive week as recovering Middle East exports and rising inventories outweighed attacks on shipping and other supply risks. Brent settled Friday at $90.75 a barrel, down 3.4% for the week, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate closed at $83.41, down 5.8%. The International Energy Agency sa
business.content: Oil prices fell for a third consecutive week as recovering Middle East exports and rising inventories outweighed attacks on shipping and other supply risks. Brent settled Friday at $90.75 a barrel, down 3.4% for the week, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate closed at $83.41, down 5.8%. The International Energy Agency said the market returned to surplus for the first time since the Iran war began, with Gulf exports recovering faster than demand. Iranian attacks on vessels around the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi strikes in Saudi Arabia have kept a geopolitical risk premium in the market. U.S. commercial crude inventories rose by 3.4 million barrels to 417.8 million in the week to Nov. 13. OPEC+ ministers are due to meet on Nov. 29 to set the group’s 2027 output policy.
business.image_alt: Oil prices post third weekly loss as Gulf exports recover

business.title: Lufthansa plans 1,000 job cuts as core airline losses persist
business.summary: Lufthansa’s flagship airline plans to cut 1,000 full-time jobs at its Frankfurt and Munich hubs, about 2.5% of its roughly 40,000 employees, as it tries to stem losses. An internal letter said the airline lost an average of €20 million a month from January through September, citing nine days of strikes, high fuel costs
business.content: Lufthansa’s flagship airline plans to cut 1,000 full-time jobs at its Frankfurt and Munich hubs, about 2.5% of its roughly 40,000 employees, as it tries to stem losses. An internal letter said the airline lost an average of €20 million a month from January through September, citing nine days of strikes, high fuel costs linked to the Iran war and an already high cost base. Lufthansa has not specified when it will cut the jobs or whether they overlap with a previously announced group-wide reduction of 4,000 mostly administrative positions. Management said the turnaround measures announced so far are no longer sufficient. The wider Lufthansa Group expects a €9.3 billion fuel bill this year, about €2 billion above 2025. Its third-quarter operating profit rose 6% to €1.4 billion, while the core airline’s operating profit fell by a third to €300 million. On Nov. 3, the group lowered its 2026 operating-profit forecast to between €1.7 billion and €2 billion, down from a maximum of €2.2 billion.
business.image_alt: Lufthansa plans 1,000 job cuts as core airline losses persist

business.title: UK retail sales rise 0.7% as households stock emergency food
business.summary: British retail sales volumes rose 0.7% in October, reversing a revised 0.6% decline in September, as households bought long-life food after the government’s Be Ready emergency-preparedness campaign and clothing sales improved in colder weather. Annual sales growth reached 2.3%, up from 0.4% in September. The increase e
business.content: British retail sales volumes rose 0.7% in October, reversing a revised 0.6% decline in September, as households bought long-life food after the government’s Be Ready emergency-preparedness campaign and clothing sales improved in colder weather. Annual sales growth reached 2.3%, up from 0.4% in September. The increase exceeded forecasts, but analysts cautioned that emergency purchases may not continue and that household budgets face renewed pressure. UK inflation reached 3.6% in October, while the Bank of England expects it to approach 5% in mid-2027; energy prices are forecast to rise by more than 20% in January. Marks & Spencer, Primark and Next reported stronger October trading, while Deloitte said growth in other non-food stores indicated Christmas gift spending had already begun.
business.image_alt: UK retail sales rise 0.7% as households stock emergency food

business.title: Gold posts worst weekly loss in eight months as rate bets rise
business.summary: Gold fell about 9% in the week to Nov. 20, its steepest weekly decline in eight months, and touched its lowest price since September 2025 as expectations of a December U.S. Federal Reserve rate increase strengthened. The U.S. dollar’s rise to a near-19-month high and elevated Treasury yields added pressure on bullion,
business.content: Gold fell about 9% in the week to Nov. 20, its steepest weekly decline in eight months, and touched its lowest price since September 2025 as expectations of a December U.S. Federal Reserve rate increase strengthened. The U.S. dollar’s rise to a near-19-month high and elevated Treasury yields added pressure on bullion, which pays no interest. A selloff in technology shares also prompted some investors to sell assets to raise cash or meet margin calls. Some analysts say leveraged selling and thin liquidity have magnified the decline, while others warn of further losses if the dollar and yields stay high. Traders are watching upcoming U.S. economic data and the Fed’s December meeting. One market analyst said a durable recovery would require stable real yields, a weaker dollar and evidence that forced selling had eased.
business.image_alt: Gold posts worst weekly loss in eight months as rate bets rise

business.title: Missouri judge approves Bayer’s $7.25 billion Roundup settlement
business.summary: A Missouri judge on Friday, Nov. 20, approved Bayer’s settlement of up to $7.25 billion to resolve claims that its Roundup weedkiller caused non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The agreement covers people already diagnosed with the disease and some who develop it in the future after exposure to Roundup; Bayer denies that Roundup cau
business.content: A Missouri judge on Friday, Nov. 20, approved Bayer’s settlement of up to $7.25 billion to resolve claims that its Roundup weedkiller caused non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The agreement covers people already diagnosed with the disease and some who develop it in the future after exposure to Roundup; Bayer denies that Roundup causes cancer. Bayer will pay into a fund annually for up to 21 years, with individual awards expected to range from $10,000 to $165,000 depending on factors including exposure, age at diagnosis and illness severity. Judge Timothy Boyer rejected objections that the awards were too low, saying delays could leave seriously ill claimants waiting years for compensation. The ruling could still be appealed.
business.image_alt: Missouri judge approves Bayer’s $7.25 billion Roundup settlement

business.title: Anthropic mathematician claims Claude helped prove Riemann hypothesis
business.summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he and the company’s Claude AI developed a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, a 167-year-old problem about prime numbers, and its broader generalization. The claim followed Anthropic’s Nov. 19 stock-market debut, when the company raised $81 billion at a $1.5 trillion valuation.
business.content: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he and the company’s Claude AI developed a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, a 167-year-old problem about prime numbers, and its broader generalization. The claim followed Anthropic’s Nov. 19 stock-market debut, when the company raised $81 billion at a $1.5 trillion valuation. Mathematicians have not yet fully examined the claimed result. Alpöge released a formalization in Lean, software that checks mathematical arguments. Massachusetts Institute of Technology mathematician Andrew Sutherland independently compiled its 175,000 files, according to a report on his review, but human mathematicians still need to assess and understand the proof’s mathematical details. Alpöge said the formalized argument exceeded 250,000 pages. He has not published a human-readable account. The announcement also prompted Stanford postdoctoral researcher Alessandro Masullo to release a separate, AI-free proof claim he said he had developed over 12 years. He warned it might contain errors because he had rushed its publication. Neither claim had been established at the time of reporting.
business.image_alt: Anthropic mathematician claims Claude helped prove Riemann hypothesis

business.title: Trump urges AI chipmaker Nvidia to reinstate Huang despite board rejection
business.summary: President Donald Trump on Friday urged U.S. AI chipmaker Nvidia to bring back co-founder Jensen Huang, who resigned as chief executive on Nov. 12 after reports of extramarital relationships, including one with a woman U.S. intelligence officials suspect has links to China. Trump said Huang should apologize and receive
business.content: President Donald Trump on Friday urged U.S. AI chipmaker Nvidia to bring back co-founder Jensen Huang, who resigned as chief executive on Nov. 12 after reports of extramarital relationships, including one with a woman U.S. intelligence officials suspect has links to China. Trump said Huang should apologize and receive a second chance, citing his role in developing Nvidia’s Blackwell chips and arguing that his leadership helped keep the United States ahead in artificial intelligence. Nvidia’s board chairman, Harvey Jones, said on Nov. 17 that directors had unanimously accepted Huang’s resignation and did not intend to reinstate him. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress is interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor. Nvidia’s market value fell from about $4.19 trillion at the Nov. 11 close to $3.14 trillion on Nov. 20, a decline of about 24.9%, although the decline cannot be attributed entirely to Huang’s departure. Nvidia chips have also reached a Singapore-based firm linked in reports to efforts to supply China.
business.image_alt: Trump urges AI chipmaker Nvidia to reinstate Huang despite board rejection

business.title: Take-Two says GTA VI generated $3.79 billion on launch day
business.summary: Publisher Take-Two Interactive said Friday that Grand Theft Auto VI, Rockstar Games’ first new entry in the crime-game series in 13 years, generated an estimated $3.79 billion in worldwide retail sales on its first day, Nov. 19. The company said it had sold 32.5 million copies before release. Based on company estimates
business.content: Publisher Take-Two Interactive said Friday that Grand Theft Auto VI, Rockstar Games’ first new entry in the crime-game series in 13 years, generated an estimated $3.79 billion in worldwide retail sales on its first day, Nov. 19. The company said it had sold 32.5 million copies before release. Based on company estimates through the end of Thursday, the total makes it the biggest entertainment launch across any medium, according to Take-Two. That figure far exceeds market research firm Sensor Tower’s earlier estimate of $2.36 billion from about 24.6 million copies and tops the $2.9 billion lifetime box-office gross attributed to Avengers: Endgame. Grand Theft Auto V, the 2013 predecessor, took three days to reach $1 billion in retail sales. Rockstar and Take-Two have not disclosed the game’s development costs, and estimates cited in coverage vary. Analysts see a possible PC release and online multiplayer as potential sources of future revenue, but Rockstar has not announced dates for either.
business.image_alt: Take-Two says GTA VI generated $3.79 billion on launch day

science.title: Global study finds glacial lakes speed ice loss; researcher urges safety oversight
science.summary: A global analysis found that glaciers ending in lakes lost ice faster from 2000 to 2020 than glaciers ending on land or at sea, while a separate paper calls for formal safety oversight of hazardous glacial lakes. Lake-terminating glaciers lost an annual average of 0.66 meters of water equivalent, compared with 0.40 met
science.content: A global analysis found that glaciers ending in lakes lost ice faster from 2000 to 2020 than glaciers ending on land or at sea, while a separate paper calls for formal safety oversight of hazardous glacial lakes. Lake-terminating glaciers lost an annual average of 0.66 meters of water equivalent, compared with 0.40 meters for land-terminating and 0.36 meters for marine-terminating glaciers. Ice-contact lakes explained an estimated 11% of mass loss among lake-terminating glaciers, compared with larger contributions from glacier geometry and climate. The study counted 3,567 more lakes in direct contact with glaciers in 2020 than in 2000, a 35% increase. University of Cambridge natural-hazards researcher Maximillian Van Wyk de Vries calls for a tiered system combining satellite screening, detailed assessments, ground monitoring and, where warranted, lake lowering. He also calls for sustained funding and local early-warning and evacuation plans.
science.image_alt: Global study finds glacial lakes speed ice loss; researcher urges safety oversight

science.title: Researchers test lunar-soil bricks and oxygen extraction methods
science.summary: University of Arkansas researchers used simulated lunar soil to print small, interlocking bricks without binders, while a separate team found that plasma treatment can release oxygen and oxygen-containing gases from lunar-soil simulants. Both experiments aim to reduce the supplies future lunar missions would need to tr
science.content: University of Arkansas researchers used simulated lunar soil to print small, interlocking bricks without binders, while a separate team found that plasma treatment can release oxygen and oxygen-containing gases from lunar-soil simulants. Both experiments aim to reduce the supplies future lunar missions would need to transport from Earth, but neither method is ready for practical use: the bricks need to be stronger, and oxygen yields must increase substantially. The brick study, published in *npj Advanced Manufacturing*, used laser powder bed fusion; the oxygen-extraction research, published in *Scientific Reports*, adapted plasma processing used in semiconductor manufacturing. Researchers still need to test the brick process in lunar vacuum and low gravity and determine whether oxygen extraction can be improved and scaled up economically.
science.image_alt: Researchers test lunar-soil bricks and oxygen extraction methods

science.title: EPFL model predicts fusion reactors’ power needs for H-mode transition
science.summary: Researchers at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne (EPFL) developed a model to estimate how much heating power tokamak fusion plasmas need to enter high-confinement mode, in which they retain energy more effectively. The model explains how plasma density and magnetic-field direction affect that thresh
science.content: Researchers at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne (EPFL) developed a model to estimate how much heating power tokamak fusion plasmas need to enter high-confinement mode, in which they retain energy more effectively. The model explains how plasma density and magnetic-field direction affect that threshold, a problem researchers have struggled to resolve since the transition was identified in 1982. For future tokamaks, the model estimates that ITER will need at least 43 megawatts, below its planned 73-megawatt capacity. For SPARC, it predicts a minimum of 26 megawatts, slightly above the planned 25 megawatts. Gizmodo notes that the model’s practical value will depend on whether other teams find it useful for their own fusion designs.
science.image_alt: EPFL model predicts fusion reactors’ power needs for H-mode transition

science.title: Astronomers track stellar merger as Andromeda giant engulfs companion
science.summary: Astronomers have reconstructed the first observed case of a giant star engulfing its companion, tracking the pair through their merger in the Andromeda Galaxy. The system, AT 2025abao, began brightening in 2018 as the smaller star spiraled through the giant’s shared envelope of gas; the plunge ended in a powerful erupt
science.content: Astronomers have reconstructed the first observed case of a giant star engulfing its companion, tracking the pair through their merger in the Andromeda Galaxy. The system, AT 2025abao, began brightening in 2018 as the smaller star spiraled through the giant’s shared envelope of gas; the plunge ended in a powerful eruption in late 2025. The study appeared in the journal Nature on Nov. 18. The analysis indicates the smaller star crashed into the giant’s core rather than surviving in a close orbit, but researchers say decades of further observations are needed to rule out a remnant. The observations recorded common-envelope evolution, a process used to explain how some binary stars tighten their orbits.
science.image_alt: Astronomers track stellar merger as Andromeda giant engulfs companion

science.title: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years without sustained transmission
science.summary: The United States has lost its measles elimination status after the same strain of the virus spread continuously for at least 12 months, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), the World Health Organization’s regional office for the Americas, announced on Nov. 17. The decision ends 26 years of elimination status,
science.content: The United States has lost its measles elimination status after the same strain of the virus spread continuously for at least 12 months, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), the World Health Organization’s regional office for the Americas, announced on Nov. 17. The decision ends 26 years of elimination status, which meant sustained transmission had stopped, not that the country had no measles cases. The US recorded more than 5,400 cases in 2026, more than twice the 2025 total. Most patients were unvaccinated or had an unknown vaccination status. Measles vaccination coverage among US kindergarteners has fallen to about 92%, below the roughly 95% needed to prevent outbreaks. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said he continues to recommend the combined measles, mumps and rubella vaccine and pledged to work to regain elimination status.
science.image_alt: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years without sustained transmission

science.title: Studies link blood and brain markers to future cognitive decline
science.summary: Three studies examined cognitive decline: a Mayo Clinic team combined the blood biomarker p-tau217 with age, sex and genetic risk to estimate five- and 10-year risk; an analysis based in Europe and the U.S. found that later-born generations had better memory and slower decline; and a Stanford-led team tested a brain-ac
science.content: Three studies examined cognitive decline: a Mayo Clinic team combined the blood biomarker p-tau217 with age, sex and genetic risk to estimate five- and 10-year risk; an analysis based in Europe and the U.S. found that later-born generations had better memory and slower decline; and a Stanford-led team tested a brain-activity score that distinguished “superagers” from people with Alzheimer’s disease. In one example from the Mayo study, a 75-year-old woman without the APOE ε4 risk variant had an estimated five-year risk of mild cognitive impairment of 5% at a lower biomarker level and 16% at a higher level. The studies do not establish that these approaches are ready for screening: the generational analysis was observational, and the brain-pattern score was less accurate in an independent cohort. Alzheimer’s biomarker testing is not currently recommended for people without cognitive symptoms.
science.image_alt: Studies link blood and brain markers to future cognitive decline

science.title: Milky Way bar shock may explain part of disputed Norma arm
science.summary: A study led by Hillary Davis, a University of Sydney PhD graduate, finds that masers assigned to the Milky Way’s Norma spiral arm align instead with a shock front driven by the galaxy’s central bar. The result suggests that at least part of the supposed arm may be a star-forming region along the bar rather than a spira
science.content: A study led by Hillary Davis, a University of Sydney PhD graduate, finds that masers assigned to the Milky Way’s Norma spiral arm align instead with a shock front driven by the galaxy’s central bar. The result suggests that at least part of the supposed arm may be a star-forming region along the bar rather than a spiral arm. The researchers compared observations of masers—microwave sources associated with regions where massive stars form—with large-scale computer simulations of galaxy evolution. Star formation is often suppressed along bar shock fronts in nearby galaxies, making the proposed activity in the Milky Way’s bar unusual. The study also constrains the bar’s dimensions and rotation speed.
science.image_alt: Milky Way bar shock may explain part of disputed Norma arm

science.title: NASA investigates Voyager 1 data outage slowed by 48-hour command cycle
science.summary: NASA engineers are investigating why Voyager 1 has stopped returning science and engineering data. The interstellar probe reached one light-day from Earth on Nov. 18. Its carrier signal remains strong, but it has returned no data since Nov. 14. NASA confirmed the distance milestone when a signal arrived at Earth 24 hou
science.content: NASA engineers are investigating why Voyager 1 has stopped returning science and engineering data. The interstellar probe reached one light-day from Earth on Nov. 18. Its carrier signal remains strong, but it has returned no data since Nov. 14. NASA confirmed the distance milestone when a signal arrived at Earth 24 hours after the spacecraft sent it. At a Nov. 19 briefing, Voyager project manager Suzanne Dodd said the spacecraft lacked “frame sync,” preventing the team from receiving its science and engineering readings. Engineers are investigating whether the fault resembles an earlier onboard-computer problem. The carrier signal indicates that the transmitter is still operating and the spacecraft remains pointed toward Earth. Each command now takes about a day to reach Voyager 1, and a response takes another day to return. The team said the long signal delay and low data rates slow diagnosis.
science.image_alt: NASA investigates Voyager 1 data outage slowed by 48-hour command cycle

sports.title: Dodgers trade for former No. 1 pick Royce Lewis to bolster infield
sports.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers acquired infielder Royce Lewis from the Minnesota Twins on Friday, Nov. 20, sending right-hander Bobby Miller and 19-year-old catching prospect Francisco Espinoza to Minnesota. Los Angeles had sought a right-handed, multi-position infielder after veteran Miguel Rojas retired. Lewis can cover fir
sports.content: The Los Angeles Dodgers acquired infielder Royce Lewis from the Minnesota Twins on Friday, Nov. 20, sending right-hander Bobby Miller and 19-year-old catching prospect Francisco Espinoza to Minnesota. Los Angeles had sought a right-handed, multi-position infielder after veteran Miguel Rojas retired. Lewis can cover first, second and third base, potentially allowing other infielders to rest. Lewis, 27, hit.227 with 15 home runs and 16 stolen bases in a career-high 125 games in 2026. His production has fallen well short of his 2023 breakout, and injuries have repeatedly interrupted his career. The Twins selected him first overall in 2017; he returns to Southern California, where he grew up. Minnesota acquired Miller, who was limited to three major-league appearances last season after shoulder problems, and added Espinoza to its farm system. Lewis remains under team control through 2028, while Miller has four years of control remaining.

sports.content: Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has defended the club’s direction and transfer strategy with the team 18th in the Premier League and new head coach Mauricio Pochettino preparing for his first game at Liverpool on Sunday. Berrada called the league position unacceptable but said the club was building for sustained competitiveness. United dismissed Michael Carrick during the November international break after a poor start, despite his having led the team to third place and Champions League qualification last season. Berrada said the club waited until the break to assess the team’s decline and concluded a coaching change could turn the season around. Pochettino has already spoken individually with players, while Berrada cited his philosophy and experience at major clubs as reasons for hiring him.

sports.content: The New York Mets have reportedly offered free-agent starting pitcher Tarik Skubal a nine-year contract worth nearly $400 million, which could set records for a pitcher’s total guarantee and average annual value. The Mets have not confirmed the offer, and Skubal is weighing interest from other clubs before a possible Major League Baseball lockout after the collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1. Skubal, who turned 30 on Nov. 20, finished 2026 with a 12-7 record, a 2.72 ERA and 186 strikeouts in 158⅔ innings despite missing several weeks for left-elbow surgery. The Mets, Los Angeles Dodgers, Toronto Blue Jays and San Diego Padres have met with him; a fifth team also reportedly held a video meeting. San Diego is targeting Michael King if Skubal signs elsewhere, while Skubal continues to weigh his options.

sports.content: Crystal Palace appointed Thomas Frank as manager on November 16, bringing the former Brentford and Tottenham coach back to the Premier League on a contract through June 2029. He takes charge with Palace bottom of the table after two wins in their first 10 league matches; they have lost four straight and conceded an average of 2.4 goals per game. Frank’s first match is Saturday’s trip to Coventry. Palace also have European and domestic cup commitments. Frank said he had reflected on his dismissal by Tottenham and learned from the experience but declined to discuss the details. At Palace, he has brought in coaches Justin Cochrane, Chris Haslam and set-piece specialist Bernardo Cueva, while assistant manager Paddy McCarthy and goalkeeping coach Andy Quy remain. Palace next host Hull in the league and Real Sociedad in the Europa League. Frank has said the Premier League must take priority if the club has to choose between competitions.

sports.content: Red Bull’s Max Verstappen will start from pole at the Las Vegas Grand Prix after newly crowned Formula 1 champion and Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli set the fastest qualifying time but received a five-place grid penalty. Antonelli clocked 1:33.893, 0.258 seconds quicker than Verstappen, but will start sixth after his team exceeded its engine-component allocation. Verstappen starts alongside Mercedes’ George Russell, who qualified third and moved up after Antonelli’s penalty. McLaren’s Lando Norris starts third. Verstappen and Russell made contact in final practice, for which Verstappen received a warning but no grid penalty. McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, seventh fastest in qualifying, drops to 17th with a 10-place engine penalty. Verstappen entered the weekend with a 17-point lead over Russell in the fight for second in the drivers’ standings, with three races remaining. The Las Vegas race is scheduled for Saturday night local time, November 21.

sports.content: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua had surgery this week to repair a knee ligament and is likely to miss the rest of the season, coach Sean McVay said Friday. McVay expects him to be out for “a couple months”. Nacua injured his knee and toe on the final play of the Rams’ Nov. 8 win over Washington and went on injured reserve four days later. McVay said the decision to operate followed medical consultations and took Nacua’s long-term performance into account. The NFL announced a three-game suspension for Nacua on Nov. 19 for a personal-conduct policy violation; he will serve it while on injured reserve. The suspension stemmed from a woman’s lawsuit alleging he made an antisemitic remark and bit her; his lawyer denied the remark and called the alleged biting “horseplay”. The 6-4 Rams face Green Bay on Nov. 25 without Nacua. McVay said fellow receiver Davante Adams is not ready to return.

Jones completed 12 of 27 passes for 144 yards and threw an interception i
sports.content: The Indianapolis Colts waived quarterback Daniel Jones on Friday, Nov. 20, and named Anthony Richardson their starter for the Nov. 29 home game against the New York Giants, less than a day after a 26-3 loss to Houston dropped Indianapolis to 3-8. Jones completed 12 of 27 passes for 144 yards and threw an interception in the defeat. Jones signed a two-year, $88 million contract in March after leading the Colts to an 8-2 start in 2025. A fibula fracture and a torn Achilles preceded a season in which he threw for 1,974 yards, seven touchdowns and 13 interceptions. His release saves Indianapolis about $11.6 million against a projected $46.8 million salary-cap hit in 2027, leaving $35.2 million in dead cap. The Colts had already fired general manager Chris Ballard and traded several veterans before the deadline. They kept Jones despite reported interest from the Minnesota Vikings and Baltimore Ravens, then released him 10 days later. Jones is subject to waivers through Monday afternoon and could choose another team if he clears. Richardson takes over as starter for a team without its 2027 first-round pick.

sports.title: Bayern Munich confirm Harry Kane will miss months with torn ankle ligament
sports.summary: Bayern Munich say striker Harry Kane will miss “the next few months” after tearing the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle during Friday’s 1-1 Bundesliga draw with Cologne. The 33-year-old was injured in a challenge while trying to reach a cross and left the field after 20 minutes. The club’s medical department conf
sports.content: Bayern Munich say striker Harry Kane will miss “the next few months” after tearing the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle during Friday’s 1-1 Bundesliga draw with Cologne. The 33-year-old was injured in a challenge while trying to reach a cross and left the field after 20 minutes. The club’s medical department confirmed the diagnosis after examining him. Bayern have seven matches across the Bundesliga, German Cup and Champions League before the winter break. An absence of roughly three months would also leave Kane’s availability for England’s two-legged Nations League quarter-final against Norway, scheduled for March 27 and 30, in doubt. Kane had scored 156 goals in 163 appearances for Bayern since joining from Tottenham in 2023 and signed a contract extension through June 2029 this month. Bayern sporting director Max Eberl said the club’s doctors were considering whether to recommend surgery. The club has not given a more precise return date.
